notes.summary: Reconstructed a conditional whole-base weak trace on the one original proper birational witness, using actual analytic discs, complete finite-fiber covering, and canonical positive norm characters. The accepted smooth geometric antecedents remain conditional.
notes.detailedSummary: For an integral affine variety finite over a principal open of affine space, the original weak trace is an original-ring decreasing affine FS limit under the task-granted contact hypotheses and retained smooth compactification/domination/resolution antecedents. The argument first extends the trace on the smooth base, then identifies every bad-fiber value using normalized horizontal curves, relative proper lifts, strict-disc radial limits, and polynomial norm-law regrouping. It includes minus-infinity values and never identifies nonflat weights with fiber lengths or invokes affine regularization over arbitrary completed residue fields.
notes.text:
This is an unverified conditional proof draft. Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued, and of characteristic zero, without a cardinality restriction. Let S=D(a) in A^n_k, let Y be integral affine, and let pi:Y→S be finite surjective of generic degree d. The original u is generically finite, usc, locally bounded above, and bounded above by Cg∘pi+B for an actual original-base affine FS exhaustion. ONE proper birational witness mu:P→Y makes its pullback locally a decreasing contact limit, with common neighborhoods and the exact same-constant unit-log support hypothesis of the task-granted round77/80 theorem.

GEO denotes the still-retained geometric antecedents in each accepted smooth-gate application: a smooth ample-boundary projective compactification and projective birational domination of the restricted original witness by a smooth projective source, with matching actual references. They are assumptions here, not newly proved geometric theorems.

The task grants the canonical polynomial norm law over the normal base. At an analytic fiber its residue characters have positive integer exponents, giving weights m_y>0 with sum d, compatible with every complete field extension. These are not nonflat lengths. For an actual finite logarithmic maximum, expansion N(sum T_i b_i)=sum a_alpha T^alpha gives the whole-base formula
sum_y m_y D^(-1)max_i(log|b_i(y)|+lambda_i)=D^(-1)max_alpha(log|a_alpha|+alpha·lambda).
The constant branch and original generators are retained.

Choose a principal dense W where pi is étale and the original witness is an isomorphism over pi^(-1)W. Primitive-element denominators, a discriminant, and the finite image of the excluded witness locus supply this open. The source there is smooth. The accepted smooth gate, retaining GEO, regularizes original u on this open. Trace its decreasing FS sequence using the displayed norm formula. Finite positive weights commute with its decreasing limit, including minus infinity. Monic equations give |z|≤max(1,max_i |a_i|^(1/(r-i))) for every integral source generator, so original source growth is controlled by the base reference. The trace has upper bound Cd g+dB. Accepted principal-open removal on the ORIGINAL smooth S gives an actual affine FS limit v extending this good-open trace. Bad values have not yet been identified.

Fix any bad analytic s and put F=H(s). Its original coordinates define an F-rational point alpha. Choose z_0 in W(k) and use the line c(t)=alpha+t(z_0-alpha), restricting to the parameter open T where chart denominators are nonzero. It contains 0 and 1. The restrictions of all good-open denominators are nonzero polynomials; hence every sufficiently small positive-radius parameter Gauss point maps into W. Their original images s_r tend to s.

Y_F is integral. Its line inverse image is cut by n−1 equations. The Noetherian height bound and finite-type domain dimension formula over F make every reduced component at least one-dimensional; finiteness over T makes it at most one-dimensional. Thus EVERY reduced component is horizontal. Normalize the whole reduction. Its components are smooth curves over the perfect characteristic-zero F, finite and flat over T by torsion freeness over base DVRs. Their total generic rank is d because the good-open inverse image is the entire original étale cover. For n=1 no cutting equations are needed; for n=0 the assertion is the direct one-point identity.

The exact primary statements used are finite normalization (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXQ), height bound (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BBZ), domain dimension formula (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02IJ), normal-curve smoothness (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B8Y), and curve flatness (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXX). Their hypotheses and complete pertinent proof units are retained in external-premises.json with nonnegative indices.

Each normalized component has a generic lift to P_F. At every closed point its DVR gives a lift by the RELATIVE valuative criterion for P_F→Y_F. Finite presentation spreads it to a neighborhood; separatedness identifies overlaps. The entire normalized curve therefore lifts to the ONE original witness. This uses https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BX4, Lemma 29.43.5, with Y_F as the base. P_F need not be proper over F.

Restrict EACH continuous contact approximant through this curve morphism before taking limits. Its support is harmonic because its logarithms are of units. The same-constant support equality gives the harmonic maximum test, and decreasing closure gives a subharmonic limit or the identically-minus-infinity alternative. The actual affine FS sequence for v gives the same conclusion for v∘c. No arbitrary-F affine theorem or positive-current pullback is used.

If F is trivial, first take an independent nontrivial Gauss extension; then pass to a completed algebraic closure L. Original pulled values are unchanged, and residue characteristic is zero because k contains trivially valued Q. At each smooth rational center choose equations F_i(z,w)=0 with invertible w-Jacobian J. On sufficiently small strict polydiscs, w↦w−J^(-1)F(z,w) preserves the disc and has Lipschitz norm less than one. Iteration converges in the Tate algebra, and the same contraction over every completed residue field proves uniqueness. Graph and projection give an ACTUAL analytic disc coordinate, not merely a formal parameter. The same argument makes z+O(z²) an analytic coordinate after shrinking.

For a pulled limit h with finite center value, a strict closed disc has one boundary Gauss point xi_R. Thuillier 3.1.9 gives its finite boundary value, and subharmonic comparison gives h(center)≤h(xi_R). Upper semicontinuity gives the reverse limiting inequality, so h(xi_R) tends to h(center). If the center value is minus infinity, usc alone gives that radial limit. Local upper bounds exclude compensating plus infinity. The exact primary statement and proof of 3.1.9 are retained from https://theses.hal.science/tel-00010990v1/document, UTF8 inclusive LF3825–3842.

Near every center the finite map is t=b z^e U(z), with U(0)=1. On a smaller disc |U−1|<1; the binomial e-th root converges in residue characteristic zero. Changing coordinate gives EXACTLY t=bz^e. Above a small strict base Gauss radius r there is one Gauss point in that center disc, of radius (r/|b|)^(1/e) and completed residue degree e. After scaling, the residue polynomial Z^e−T is irreducible over the residue Gauss field; the finite extension has degree e and its absolute value is unique.

These discs cover the ENTIRE sufficiently small finite Gauss fiber. Indeed, fix a compact finite preimage of one strict base disc. Its closed complement outside all center neighborhoods, intersected with successively smaller closed base discs, is a decreasing family of compact sets with empty intersection. Compactness makes one empty. No unseen branch remains.

The original norm law pulled to T and the product determinant norm of all normalized horizontal curves agree over the dense good open. Both have regular polynomial coefficients on the integral parameter ring, so they agree at 0. A center of ramification order e and residue field kappa contributes e[kappa:F]. Equality of residue characters, followed by complete-field compatibility, groups these contributions into precisely the ORIGINAL canonical m_y, not nonflat fiber dimensions.

For small strict radii, v(s_r) equals the sum of all branch values with these degrees. Apply the strict radial limit to the left and every branch. Finite center values permit finite summation; one minus-infinity center makes the sum tend to minus infinity because its coefficient is positive and all other terms are bounded above. Regrouping proves v(s)=sum_{y|s}m_y u(y) at EVERY original analytic s. This completes the whole-base trace application under GEO, including exceptional, nonflat, removed, and minus-infinity values.

notes.summary: Reconstructed controlled approximation for already genuine singular affine FS limits, corrected pole control by finite normalization and one uniform original-ring multiplier, and supplied the countable entropy barrier, Rossi principle, and off-bad-set inequality without singular EP.
notes.detailedSummary: The approximation starts with actual decreasing affine FS approximants and uses reference-winning expanding collars in one genuine bundle, retaining every original generator. Height-one bounds make h=b^N f^(Nc/q) integral; finite R[h] supplies one f^M clearing every h^j into the original ring, and roots recover hull bounds. Rational entropy-grid roofs give global majorants on every coordinate face; interval coefficient maxima and decreasing generator padding include unbounded and minus-infinity support replacements. Off-bad-set control assumes regularizability of the original u, not merely u+c rho.
notes.text:
This is an unverified proof draft using the exact task-granted continuous contact/model/nef/FS bridge and genuine decreasing closure. Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued, characteristic zero, and R an integral finite-type k-algebra. Countability is required only for the barrier. Actual affine FS expressions retain a rational constant floor and a positive-slope branch for EVERY original generator.

Controlled approximation G starts with an ALREADY supplied decreasing affine FS sequence v_j→v and v≤g+B, where g≥0 is an actual rational FS exhaustion. Compactify its actual reference by clearing slopes and embedding with their integer powers AND every unpowered original generator at dominated low weights. The standard chart is consequently the ORIGINAL Spec R. Write g=g_0+p for the actual reference bundle and global FS potential.

Fix rational c>1. Choose C_i decreasing to minus infinity and R_i increasing to infinity with (c−1)R_i>B−C_i+2. On compact Q_i={g≤R_i}, nested closed superlevel emptiness supplies indices j_i increasing with v_{j_i}<g+B+1. Define a_i=max(v_{j_i},cg+C_i) on Q_i and cg+C_i outside. The reference wins on a WHOLE outer collar. Its canonical potential is a_i−cg_0, including cp on the boundary; omitting p would change the reference. The granted bridge gives genuine membership in the same bundle cB_ref.

These weights decrease on the old region because both branches decrease, on the new annulus because g+B+1<cg+C_i, and on the exterior because floors decrease. Their limit is v on Y and minus infinity at the boundary. Genuine closure establishes membership BEFORE same-class sequential FS regularization. In the boundary-section frame this gives w_i decreasing to v, with |w_i−cg| bounded for each i and one common upper bound cg+B'. Alternatively uniformly approximate a_i with errors epsilon_i=4^(−i) and shifts 2 sum_{r≥i}epsilon_r; consecutive shift gaps dominate both errors. Original section localization converts weights to R, and dominated sections representing every original generator plus a constant floor change no values. G requires no singular EP.

The printed denominator-order claim fails already for f=x²,p=x. With b=p/f=1/x and q=3/2, q log|b|≤max(0,log|f^(-1)|), while q times the displayed denominator exponent is 3/2>1. Taking G=max(0,log|x|) retains the original generator and preserves the growth hypothesis.

The replacement is as follows. Suppose q log|b|≤max(G,c log|f^(-1)|)+B_0, with b in R_f and q,c positive rational. Choose N so m=Nc/q is integral and put h=b^N f^m. In the finite normalization Rbar, every height-one valuation E containing f gives analytic seminorms exp(−t ord_E). Original regular functions have norm at most one, so G has a bound independent of t. Dividing the growth inequality by t gives q ord_E(b)+c ord_E(f)≥0. Thus h is nonnegative at these valuations, and is regular at all other height-one primes. The height-one intersection theorem makes h integral over R. The exact primary statements are https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXQ, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/031T, and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00PD, with finite-type, normal Noetherian, and DVR hypotheses retained.

R[h] is a finite R-module contained in R_f. Clearing denominators of ONE finite module generating list gives ONE f^M with f^M h^j in ORIGINAL R for EVERY j≥0. This does not assert h itself belongs to R. For example, in R=k[t²,t³], f=t² and h=t is integral but outside R; f h^j=t^(j+2) belongs to R for all j, since every integer at least two is generated by two and three.

For compact L in Y_f and x in its ORIGINAL polynomial hull intersect Y_f, test all f^M h^j. Taking j-th roots gives |h(x)|≤sup_L|h|; a zero supremum is handled directly. If |log|f||≤M_1 on L union {x}, substitution gives q log|b(x)|≤sup_L q log|b|+2cM_1. This applies branchwise to finite maxima, including their floor. For an already genuine v on Y_f bounded by an original reference, apply G to g_c=max(g,c log|f^(-1)|), retaining original generators and f^(-1). Controlled approximants have bound 2g_c+B', hence hull error 4cM_1. Compact nested-superlevel emptiness gives sup_L w_i→sup_L v, even when the latter is minus infinity. Let i increase and c decrease to zero. The exact conclusion is v(x)≤sup_L v. Dini for discontinuous limits is not used.

For the countable barrier enumerate all f_i in R, keeping original generators z_l. On s coordinates t in (R union {+infinity})^s use rational beta≥log(s+1) and chi_s(t)=beta^(-1)log(1+sum exp(−beta t_i)), with exp(−beta infinity)=0. It lies between max(0,−t_i) and that maximum plus one. At a point, finite coordinates have positive probabilities p_i and the constant coordinate has p_0>0; infinite coordinates receive zero coefficients. The support ell=−sum p_i t_i+C has the SAME value there, lies below chi, and has a uniform positive gap outside any neighborhood. On the finite face the recession expression max(0,−a_i)+sum p_i a_i is positive for every nonzero a, hence the gap is coercive. On omitted-coordinate faces, leaving a neighborhood of infinity contributes a uniformly positive exponential term. The all-infinity face has support zero.

For rational approximation use E(p)=beta^(-1)sum p_i log p_i on the compact probability simplex. Triangulate by rational grids respecting EVERY face. Choose rational vertex heights h_p in [E(p),E(p)+epsilon]. Their convex roof is between E and E+delta, with delta tending to zero by uniform continuity and shrinking mesh. Conjugation gives rational maxima H_r(x)=max_grid(p·x−h_p)+delta_r satisfying chi_s(−x)≤H_r(x)≤chi_s(−x)+delta_r GLOBALLY. When x_i=−infinity only the face p_i=0 remains; its grid gives the SAME bound. Rational positive slopes clear to original monomial logarithms. Summable shifts make the approximants decrease.

Put rho_j=chi_{k+j} applied to the original generators and first j enumerated functions. Polynomial degree bounds give rho_j≤D_j g+1 and rho_j≥g, where g=max(0,log|z_l|). Choose positive rational gamma_j with gamma_j(D_j+1)≤2^(−j). Then rho=sum gamma_j rho_j is finite continuous, nonnegative, locally uniformly convergent, and ≤g+1. Upper partial sums sum_{j≤r}gamma_j rho_j+2^(−r)(g+1) decrease. Rational approximations and summable shifts produce an actual decreasing original FS sequence.

For x in an open U, choose one finite enumerated-coordinate neighborhood contained in U and replace that rho_j by its support ell. Keep all other positive summands. This explicitly constructs rho'≤rho, equality at x, and rho'≤rho−delta outside U. It may be unbounded below or minus infinity. Positivity is proved from the displayed sum, never by subtracting psh.

For a positive real coefficient a log|f|, nested positive rational intervals a_r increasing to a and b_r decreasing to a give max(a_r log|f|,b_r log|f|) decreasing to a log|f|, including zeros and minus infinity. Zero coefficients are omitted; constants decrease rationally to their targets. The other positive summands use the same countable tail bounds and shifts. Append epsilon_r g−r, with positive rational epsilon_r decreasing to zero, to retain a constant floor and EVERY original generator. This decreases and tends to minus infinity at every fixed point, preserving all limit values. No uniform convergence is claimed at minus-infinity points. Principal localization uses the same construction with every new generator, including f^(-1).

Polynomial hulls are compact: original generator inequalities place them in a compact affine polydisc domain. Their FS hulls are identical by branchwise inequalities and an original polynomial separator padded with low generator branches. A compact polynomially convex K inside an open U admits a strict finite polynomial neighborhood Q with compact controlled closure P inside U: finitely many separators on an ambient bounded complement provide rational strict margins. Strict polynomial domains are Runge because compact-subset suprema remain strictly below every constraint. Their interiors are not called compact, and arbitrary weak-inequality interiors are not identified with strict domains.

Rossi is proved directly. For z in hull(L) outside L and relatively compact V with closure disjoint from L, set K_V=boundary(V) intersect hull(L). If log|f(z)|>t>sup_{K_V}log|f|, choose nonnegative original FS g_0 zero near hull(L), with its zero-polytope avoiding the bad boundary part. It has a positive lower bound on that compact part. A large rational C makes Cg_0>log|f|−t on the WHOLE boundary. Glue their maximum inside V to Cg_0 outside. The whole collar is reference-winning. The granted bridge gives uniform same-bundle original FS approximation of this compact modification. Its value is zero on L and positive at z, contradicting the FS hull. Thus z belongs to hull(K_V).

Finally assume ORIGINAL u is locally genuinely regularizable off Z. This cannot be replaced by a hypothesis only on u+c rho, since subtracting psh is unavailable. If u_c violates the hull inequality off Z, add a small positive rational multiple of max log|f_i| for the ideal of Z. A finite attained hull maximum then occurs outside Z union L. Choose a controlled principal chart there, replace rho by rho' with its boundary gap, and form w=u+c rho'+epsilon max log|f_i|. ORIGINAL local regularizability and the positive constructions make w genuine on that chart, with original global upper growth. Rossi puts its maximum point in the original hull of the boundary intersection; corrected principal-open hull control contradicts the gap c delta. For Z empty omit the ideal term. This proves the off-bad-set inequality.

notes.summary: Reconstructed the conditional countable-field split-piece, descending-Z, Runge/Hartogs, finite-projection, and singular-stratum chain, including gamma=1 and the final empty-Z local-to-global step. It does not establish arbitrary-cardinality singular EP.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1 and n2, the split contradiction fixes one neighborhood where the integer branch sum is constant, retains raw positive weights and c times the boundary gap, and uses a closed immersion for analytic injectivity. Hartogs begins with genuine Runge exhaustion and then proves the strict coefficient-radius formula, including infinity. Componentwise dimension drop, exact finite localization, smooth-stratum projection, and singular induction yield conditional countable affine regularization. All accepted smooth geometric witnesses remain conditional; resolved-nef fiber descent and target EP are still missing.
notes.text:
This is an unverified conditional proof draft using n1 and n2. Retain countable algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k, integral affine Y, an original generically finite upper-growth weak u, ONE proper birational contact witness, and GEO for every accepted smooth-gate application. Countability does not replace the original arbitrary-cardinality target.

First suppose pi:Y→S is finite onto a principal open of A^n, pi|Z is a CLOSED IMMERSION, and Z and Z'=pi^(-1)(pi(Z)) outside Z are disjoint closed. ORIGINAL u is locally genuinely regularizable off Z. If {u+c rho<0} is not Runge, choose compact L and normalize its hull maximum to zero, with sup_L u_c≤−delta<0. The maximum x is in Z by n2.

The hull C of {pi(x)} is inside pi(Z), by the quotient-ring hull property. Its entire finite preimage splits into compact pieces C_1 in Z and C_2 in Z'. Disjoint neighborhoods A_1,A_2 and properness give a base neighborhood A of ALL C whose entire preimage lies in their union. Choose actual base FS g≥0, zero on an inner strict neighborhood U of C, with {g≤1} compactly contained in A. W={g<1} has open clopen preimage pieces W_i; only their controlled closures are compact.

The indicator of W_1 has continuous canonical trace over U, an integer gamma_1(s)=sum_{fiber intersect W_1}m_y. It is only locally constant. Shrink ONE neighborhood N of pi(x) where it is a positive integer gamma, and keep EVERY later boundary and fiber test inside N. A closed immersion remains one after completed field extension, guaranteeing analytic fiber injectivity. The W_1 fiber above pi(x) is exactly x.

For gamma>1, usc at that unique point and properness shrink N so every W_1 fiber value of u_c is less than delta/[2(gamma−1)]. For gamma=1 no division is made: positivity and integrality mean every W_1 fiber has one point of weight one.

Choose relatively compact V around x with closure in pi^(-1)(N) intersect W_1, disjoint from L. Let K_V=boundary(V) intersect hull(L). Replace rho by rho' with equality at x and gap delta' on the boundary. Then u'_c=u+c rho' is zero at x and at most −c delta' on K_V. Put v=u'_c on W_1 and zero on W_2. These have a finite upper bound M on the controlled closure. For rational C_0>M+1+delta, glue max(C_0 g∘pi−delta,v) on the preimage of W to its reference outside. The reference wins on the WHOLE outer collar; restrictions, products and maxima retain the SAME witness. Over U the resulting tilde v is max(u'_c,−delta) on W_1 and zero on W_2.

By n1, w=N_pi tilde v is a genuine base AFS limit. Pullback is a genuine original-source AFS limit; monic generator bounds and decreasing low padding retain EVERY source generator. Rossi gives x in hull(K_V), hence w(pi(x))≤sup_{K_V}w∘pi. The left side is zero. On K_V intersect Z, its unique W_1 fiber has weight gamma, giving the upper bound −gamma min(delta,c delta'). At y in K_V outside Z, n2 gives u_c(y)≤−delta, so its own tilde v value is −delta. For gamma>1 all other W_1 values are bounded by delta/[2(gamma−1)], within the SAME N. With its raw weight m_y≥1 the trace is at most −m_y delta+(gamma−m_y)delta/[2(gamma−1)]≤−delta/2. For gamma=1 there is no other point and the trace is −delta. W_2 contributes zero. Uniform negativity on ALL K_V contradicts Rossi. Thus every translated strict sublevel of u_c is Runge. Rational c decreasing to zero gives {u<0} as an increasing union of Runge opens, since rho is finite nonnegative.

Hartogs starts only AFTER a Runge domain has been proved. Countable R makes the seminorm topology second countable. Generator-bounded compact domains give local compactness and a compact exhaustion. For a Runge open D, inductively hull the next compact set together with the previous closure, then use n2's strict polynomial neighborhoods. This yields increasing STRICT polynomial opens Q_r with compact controlled closures inside D and union D. Every original generator is bounded among their constraints. We do not identify arbitrary closed-polytope interiors with strict inequalities.

For a Runge D in (Y×A¹)^an containing the zero section, write its Q_r constraints as log|sum_i a_{rji}w^i|<b_{rj}, with ORIGINAL coefficients in R and rational b. Zero lies in Q_r over Omega_r={log|a_{rj0}|<b_{rj} for all j}; these opens increase and cover Y. Over y in Omega_r the EXACT open-disc radius is
−log d_r(y)=max_{j,i≥1}(log|a_{rji}(y)|−b_{rj})/i.
Zero coefficients give minus infinity; an empty maximum means radius infinity. Strict constant-coefficient inequalities are essential.

Indeed, at every positive real radius s the polynomial Gauss norm is max_i |a_i|s^i, including radii outside the value group. It bounds every point of the closed disc. Consequently an open radius r is contained in all strict constraints exactly when every positive-degree |a_i|r^i≤exp(b_j); endpoint equality is harmless because the endpoint is excluded. A larger disc contains a violating Gauss point. This proves the formula over EVERY H(y), using polynomial norms rather than an affine theorem there.

The radii increase to d_D: every closed fiber disc of radius s<d_D is compact in D and hence lies in some Q_r. This includes d_D=infinity. Thus A_r=−log d_r decreases to u_D. A retained w-bound supplies a constant floor for each A_r. If u_D is generically finite and bounded by original g+B, choose increasing reference compacts inside the eventual Omega_r and indices with A_r<g+B+1 there, using nested compact-superlevel emptiness. Glue max(A_r,cg+C_i) to cg+C_i outside. The old-region, new-annulus and exterior arguments of G give a globally decreasing continuous contact sequence in ONE actual bundle. The granted bridge and genuine closure establish membership BEFORE FS regularization. Section localization and padding give an ORIGINAL coefficient-ring sequence retaining EVERY original generator. Infinity gives minus infinity correctly.

For original u, H=log|w|+u∘p on Y×A¹ has the SAME product witness P×A¹. Restrict each contact approximant, floor log|w| on common neighborhoods, and then take limits; define H=minus infinity at w=0 or u=minus infinity. Product-reference growth retains all generators and w. On good affine charts ORIGINAL regularizability of u gives actual regularizability of H by positive sums and padding. The split argument applies to pi×identity and Z×A¹, and proves D={H<0} genuinely Runge in the PRODUCT. It contains zero and d_D=exp(−u), including infinity. Hartogs therefore regularizes original u. Product Runge is not inferred merely from Y-sublevels.

Now remove the disjoint-piece hypothesis. Define reduced Z_1=Z and Z_{r+1}=Z_r intersect closure_Y(pi^(-1)(pi(Z_r)) outside Z_r). Closed immersion makes component images distinct and incomparable. Each component of Z_r is a component of the full inverse image: a containing component has a containing image, and finiteness preserves dimension, forcing equality. Thus the complementary closure omits every component's generic point, and maximum dimension strictly drops until empty. Outside pi^(-1)(pi(Z_{r+1})), the complementary piece is closed; its only added closure points on Z_r were in Z_{r+1}.

Inductively assume ORIGINAL local regularizability off Z_r. A point in pi^(-1)(pi(Z_{r+1})) outside Z_{r+1} is off ORIGINAL Z by closed-immersion injectivity, so the initial good cover applies. At any other new point choose principal S' in S outside pi(Z_{r+1}) and set U=pi^(-1)(S') EXACTLY. Its bad piece and complementary inverse-image piece are disjoint closed. Apply the split proof to U×A¹, obtain genuine product Runge, and apply Hartogs to regularize u on U. This proves the next induction stage.

At the final empty Z, a cover by closed-point neighborhoods covers ALL scheme points because finite-type schemes over a field are Jacobson (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0478); it consequently covers all analytic points. A local cover alone is insufficient. Apply n2 with EMPTY bad set to prove sublevels Runge, then apply the SAME empty-bad-set argument to H on the product and use Hartogs. This is the required final LOCAL-TO-GLOBAL step.

The finite projection along a smooth stratum is also reconstructed. Embed a projective closure X of integral affine Y in P^D with D≥n+1. Put T=closure_X Z union boundary, reduced, of dimension at most n−1 and smooth at the tested closed k-point z. Choose a projection center outside X, the closed secant cone from z to T outside z, and its tangent space. Their dimensions are below D, so such a k-point exists. Projection is finite by https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B1P; secant/tangent avoidance gives a single T-fiber and injective differential, following the primary argument at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B1Q.

For the possibly reducible T, the local algebra supplies the additional proof. Let C be its image local ring and D_T the finite local algebra above it. The single fiber has residue k. Cotangent surjectivity gives m_D=m_C D+m_D², hence m_D=m_C D by Nakayama. Then D/m_C D=k, so Nakayama for the finite C-module gives D=C. Projection is an isomorphism near the tested image. Repeating projection preserves this local smoothness until ambient P^n; X maps onto P^n. Because boundary was included in T, the image of z avoids the boundary image. Choose principal affine S inside the isomorphism neighborhood and away from that image, and set U=r^(-1)(S). This CORRECT U is affine inside ORIGINAL Y; pi:U→S is finite onto and pi|Z_U is an isomorphism onto a closed image, guaranteeing analytic injectivity after every field extension. This proves the finite-projection step, but not GEO's separate resolution/compactification antecedents.

Finally take successive REDUCED singular loci Y_0=Y, Y_{r+1}=sing(Y_r). Over characteristic zero their smooth regular locus is dense in every component (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B8X), so dimensions drop to empty. The accepted smooth gate gives the first local stage, retaining GEO and the original restricted witness.
